subject.title: [Bug]: Potential resource leak in runBoundTurnWithMissingThreadRecovery -- retry not wrapped in try/finally after thread spawn

question: Should Codex app-server conversation bindings unsubscribe the bound thread after every turn/retry, or should subscriptions remain persistent with a different cleanup owner?
rationale: The source-level leak is clear, but a blanket unsubscribe policy changes the lifecycle contract for bound conversation threads and needs an owner decision before automation rewrites it.

options.title: Per-turn cleanup with reattach semantics
options.body: Add best-effort unsubscribe for bound app-server turns, including replacement-thread retry failure, and cover later turns by resuming or reattaching before use.

options.title: Persistent subscription owner
options.body: Keep bound-thread subscriptions persistent but add a documented owner, sweeper, or diagnostic so replacement-thread failures cannot strand unknown subscriptions.

options.title: Live evidence first
options.body: Require instrumentation or a live repro before changing lifecycle behavior, accepting the current source-level risk for now.

recommendation.title: Per-turn cleanup with reattach semantics
recommendation.body: Add best-effort unsubscribe for bound app-server turns, including replacement-thread retry failure, and cover later turns by resuming or reattaching before use.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Codex binding refactors and harness maintenance make this the best available routing candidate for the lifecycle decision.
